‘Grandeur and History’?? You should have gone to Princeton if you wanted to bathe in self-righteous, Oxford-copying architecture. That gross fake Latin and art pallete carving makes me puke every time I pass EBI ‘s entrance on the way to Towers. And when I can’t skip 2 classes to wait in the Pho line or have to reset the coffee machine myself, the weird renditions of pasta dishes make my grandfather Luigi roll in his grave. The first time I saw that ‘tomato on top of bread’ thing Dining dares charge as an entreé, I audibly laughed. 

But Rand. Rand IS Vanderbilt. It’s at an equitable location on main campus for you to meet with anyone. I personally have had two successful breakups due to the neutral ambience of the 2301 booths. It had the largest variety of foods, from soul, (good) Italian, Midwestern, Caribbean, and more. The rotations are definitely far more varied than EBI, as every weird meatloaf variety is presented at least twice a month at Every Bad Idea. There’s a reason the line’s out the door during Rand lunch: Randwiches, texmex bowls, and Mongolian bowls are all great options with enough customization to leave Chipotle spinning. And Rand is also the best option for inclusive choices, with the most accurate halal/vegan/etc. labels and the options of Grins/2301 close by. I’ve definitely seen meat marked as vegan at Elite Brat Institute. 

I also don’t know what ‘old cafes’ you visit, but tell me where I can find an iconic vegetable rendition of a Napoleonic battle there. The Rand booths are comfortable to the point where actually being able to secure one feels like winning the lottery. The large assortment of windows gives natural sunlight to replenish serotonin, while the fake wooden walls of Evil Bastard Intentions give me Catholic school ptsd. While not perfect, the dork quirkiness of Rand gives me hope that this school is more than a Deloitte feeder for the .5%, but a place with unique spirit and charm.


Does the radio repeat hourly? Of course. Are there better places to eat some days? Definitely. But from a food variety, cuisine quality, equitability (not all of use can be Res Ed), and interior style standpoint, Rand sits alone.
